title.narrative: Tripartite constituents effectively address challenges in the future of work, especially relating to the digital transformation in line with ILS

description.narrative: While digitalization and AI in China have boosted employment flexibility, they have also created new labour market challenges, including unclear employment relationships, inadequate protection for non-standard workers, and inadaqute social dialogue mechanisms. The ILO has assisted tripartite constituents in strengthening labour policies for protecting workers in the digital economy, building capacity and advancing decent work in digital economy. In 2026–27, ILO will support tripartite constituents to further strengthen their capacity to tackle future of work challenges brought by digital transformation, in line with international labour standards. This includes better evidence-based policy making and inclusive social dialogue on defining employment relationships, protecting non-standard and platform workers, and governing digital technologies and AI to advance decent work and social justice. Expected results include: Enhanced capacity of tripartite constituents to address employment relationship determination in line with international labour standards; Improved labour protection policies for workers in non-standard forms of employment by tripartite partners; Strengthened evidence-based policy dialogue on the impacts of digital technologies and artificial intelligence on China’s labour market and working conditions; Developed and shared policy recommendations on artificial intelligence and its impacts on the future of work in China; Improved social dialogue mechanisms in the platform economy, with increased understanding of collective bargaining and algorithmic governance; Increased visibility and shared good practices on innovative applications of digital technologies and artificial intelligence in labour governance in China.
